prompt: In the style of Dungeons & Dragons official book illustration — high quality, high fidelity, digitally painted: A group of eight adventurers stand in the deep jungle with their backs to the viewer, looking up at Kir Sabal — a clifftop monastery built into a sheer jungle mountain face. They are in the foreground, casually grouped, indistinct silhouettes in traveling gear. No dramatic reactions — just tired, road-worn people taking in what they're seeing. High above, barely visible on an upper terrace, a young woman stands alone looking down at them. She is small in the frame — distinguished by her stillness and straight posture rather than any glow or light. No radiance. Just a figure watching. Kir Sabal fills the background: weathered white stone structures stacked at different elevations up the cliff face, a grand domed roof at the peak, wooden scaffolding and rope bridges connecting terraced dwellings, waterfalls trickling down the rock face on either side. Mist clings to the mountain. The jungle canopy stretches far below. A few aarakocra — large eagle-headed bird-people — circle silently in the grey-gold sky. Late afternoon light, diffuse and hazy. No single dramatic light source. The mood is quiet, uncertain, and vast.
